facts.label: reported
facts.quote: On Tuesday, Marvel released the final trailer for the upcoming Avengers movie, and it generated 563 million views in the first 24 hours.
facts.text: The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday accumulated 563 million views across platforms in its first 24 hours.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Marvel will release the film on Dec. 18, 2026, and these moments give audiences their clearest look at it until then.
facts.text: Marvel Studios has scheduled the theatrical release of Avengers: Doomsday for December 18, 2026.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The report also says Chris Evans and Chris Hemsworth could each earn around $40 million for their roles in the upcoming Avengers films, while the two films' combined production budgets are reportedly around $600 million.
facts.text: The combined production budget for the two upcoming Avengers films is reported to be around $600 million.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: In July 2024, Variety reported that the Russo brothers would receive $80 million to direct the two Avengers films, with additional performance-based bonuses.
facts.text: Directors Anthony and Joe Russo are reportedly receiving $80 million to direct the two back-to-back Avengers films.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: According to Variety's 2024 report, the actor had earned an estimated $500 million to $600 million from his MCU appearances, including four Avengers movies, the Iron Man trilogy and supporting appearances in other Marvel films.
facts.text: Robert Downey Jr. earned between $500 million and $600 million from his previous appearances across the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: International ticket sales and home entertainment help, but theaters typically keep around half of every ticket sold, and production budgets don't include marketing costs.
facts.text: Movie theatres typically keep roughly half of every ticket sold at the box office, while production budgets exclude marketing expenses entirely.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: By the common industry rule of thumb that a film needs to gross about 2.5 times its production budget to break even in theaters, it's quite possible that only Coraline, buoyed by a blockbuster 2024 rerelease, has cleared that bar.
facts.text: A standard film industry rule of thumb requires a movie to gross around 2.5 times its production budget globally to achieve theatrical break-even.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: According to the final settlement, 50, 42, 35 and 30 percent of collections in the first, second, third and fourth weeks respectively will be shared between the two parties.
facts.text: In Indian multiplex agreements, ticket collections in the first week are divided evenly at 50 percent between producers and theatre operators.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The base revenue limit that exhibitors are seeking implies that any film collecting between ₹ 30 crore and ₹ 35 crore at the box office would earn the producer/distributor 50% of the revenue in week one, falling to 42.5%, 37.5% and 30% in the subsequent three weeks.
facts.text: In the standard sliding revenue scale used by Indian multiplexes, the producer's share falls to 42.5 percent during the second week of screening.
